meta.title: SolarPunk Knowledge Base
meta.description: Verified, active, replicable SolarPunk projects worldwide. Updated March 2026.
meta.maintained_by: Meeko Nerve Center — Gaza Rose Gallery

projects.name: Solar North — Tll Yahda Energy
projects.description: Indigenous-owned and operated 2MW solar plant + microgrid. Flipped on December 5, 2025. Path to 100% diesel-free energy by 2030 for Haida Nation.
how_to_replicate: Form a band council or First Nation energy authority with legal authority to sign PPAs
Negotiate a Community Electricity Purchase Agreement (CEPA) with provincial grid operator
Procure solar + battery storage for grid-forming microgrid — start with 500kW pilot
Apply for Indigenous Clean Energy grants (Canada: INAC; US: DOE Tribal Energy Program)
Hire locally — target 75%+ Indigenous labour hours
Document diesel displacement monthly — builds case for expansion funding

projects.name: Mino Giizis Solar — Good Sun
projects.description: Four First Nations hold 50/50 equity in a 100MW solar farm. Not a benefit agreement — ownership. Mino Giizis means 'good sun' in Anishinaabemowin.
how_to_replicate: Find private renewable developer willing to do true equity partnership — not revenue sharing
Structure as Limited Partnership or JV — Nations hold 50% equity from day one
Negotiate 25-year PPA with provincial utility (Crown corporation as offtaker)
Require 75% Indigenous labour hours in all construction contracts
Apply to Canada's Indigenous Loan Guarantee Program for project financing

projects.name: Canada's Largest Indigenous-Owned Solar

metrics.model: First Indigenous developer to supply directly to industrial customer via grid

projects.description: CAD $84M, 100% Indigenous-owned. First private Indigenous developer to supply electricity to an industrial customer via SaskPower grid under a 30-year PPA. A model that previously didn't legally exist.
how_to_replicate: Identify industrial energy buyer needing long-term price certainty (mining, agriculture, manufacturing)
Structure PPA so buyer pays Nation directly via grid — negotiate wheeling fees with utility
100% Indigenous ownership requires Indigenous Development Finance Corporation for equity financing
Document as first-of-kind — create the legal path for the next Nation to follow

projects.name: Northern Cheyenne Off-Grid Buffalo Solar
projects.description: Complete off-grid solar + battery system for remote buffalo caretaking site. Zero grid connection. The herd returns. The sun powers the work.
how_to_replicate: Identify remote cultural/agricultural sites using diesel generators
Size solar + battery for actual load (caretaking sites: 5-20kW, 2-3 days storage)
Contact Indigenized Energy — they specialize in exactly this
Apply to USDA Rural Energy for America Program (REAP) — up to 50% grants
Document cultural significance — funding bodies respond to the full story

projects.name: NYC Community Land Trust Movement
projects.description: From 2 CLTs 12 years ago to 20+ across all five boroughs. Permanently removes land from speculative market. Now paired with solar, green roofs, and stormwater systems as climate infrastructure.
how_to_replicate: Form 501(c)(3) nonprofit with tripartite board: 1/3 residents, 1/3 community, 1/3 public interest
Acquire land through city disposition, donation, or purchase
Use ground lease model: CLT owns land, homeowner occupies with 99-year renewable ground lease
Include resale formula in every ground lease — caps appreciation permanently
Apply to LIHTC or HOME Investment Partnerships Program for construction financing
Contact Grounded Solutions Network — they train and support new CLTs

projects.name: Denver Urban Gardens — Food Forest Network
projects.description: 20+ publicly accessible food forests across Denver. Multi-layered perennial ecosystems — fruit trees, berry bushes, perennial vegetables, edible groundcovers. Free to harvest. Minimum maintenance. Permanent public infrastructure.
how_to_replicate: Identify available public land — approach city parks with formal proposal using 7-layer forest garden model
Design with guild system: canopy → understory → shrubs → groundcover → roots → vines
Apply to USDA Community Food Projects Competitive Grant — up to $400K
Form maintenance collective — 10-15 stewards sustain 1 acre with monthly workdays
Contact Denver Urban Gardens for technical assistance
Document yields and share openly — your data seeds the next food forest

projects.name: Chicago Wealth Our Way — Co-op Grants
projects.description: $2M in grants (not loans) to worker cooperatives and shared-ownership businesses on Chicago's South and West sides. Manufacturing center, live-work housing for young Black Chicagoans.
how_to_replicate: File as Worker Cooperative Corporation or multi-member LLC with cooperative bylaws
Structure governance: one member, one vote regardless of capital
Contact USFWC for legal templates and technical assistance
Apply to CDFI Fund for CDFI status — unlocks co-op grant programs
Find city/county solidarity economy offices — Chicago, NYC, Boston, Oakland have dedicated co-op development programs

projects.name: Essence 2.0 — Cooperative Grid Cybersecurity
projects.description: DOE $6M grant to electric cooperatives (the most community-owned segment of the US energy grid) for shared cybersecurity infrastructure. Mutual aid tech for grid resilience.
how_to_replicate: Electric cooperatives are member-owned nonprofits — you pay in, you own a share, you vote
Form energy cooperative under your state's Electric Cooperative Act
Apply to USDA Rural Development Electric Program for low-interest loans
Pool cybersecurity resources across cooperatives via shared services agreements
Contact NRECA for formation support

projects.name: Zenzeleni Networks — Community-Owned Internet, South Africa
projects.description: Africa's first community-owned ISP. Rural Eastern Cape village owns and operates its own mesh internet cooperative. 90% cheaper than commercial telecoms. Model now replicating across 6 African countries.
how_to_replicate: Map your community's connectivity gaps with a simple survey
Register a cooperative under local cooperative law — minimum 7 founding members
Buy secondhand WiFi routers (TP-Link or Ubiquiti) — $50-150 each for mesh nodes
Apply for community telecom license (South Africa: ICASA; contact APC for your country)
Install solar panels on mesh nodes for off-grid resilience
Charge members $1-3/month — covers hardware maintenance and expansion
Contact Zenzeleni for replication playbook: zenzeleni.net

projects.name: iNethi Community Network — Cape Town

metrics.model: community network with local content hosting

projects.description: Community-built mesh network in Cape Town township. Includes local content servers so residents can access education, health info, and entertainment without internet bills. Open-source stack.
how_to_replicate: Use LibreRouter or Raspberry Pi as mesh nodes — full open-source firmware
Set up a local content server (Raspberry Pi + external SSD, ~$100) for offline content
Load it with Khan Academy, Wikipedia, local health guides via Kiwix
Build community governance: elected tech committee, monthly meetings
Apply to Internet Society Community Networks program for seed funding
GitHub: iNethi stack is fully open-source at github.com/inethi

projects.name: Humbo Community Forest — Ethiopia
projects.description: Community-managed reforestation using Farmer-Managed Natural Regeneration (FMNR). 2,728 hectares restored. Community earns carbon credits ($300K+). Wildlife returned. UN Development Award winner.
how_to_replicate: Map degraded land — identify areas where native tree stumps still exist (FMNR works best here)
Form a community forest cooperative with elected ranger committees
Register with a carbon credit standard (Gold Standard or Verra VCS) — World Vision can advise
Train community members to select, protect, and prune regenerating shoots
Sell verified carbon credits — expect $5-15/tonne, ~10 tonnes/hectare restored
Reinvest revenue: 40% to individual farmers, 40% to community fund, 20% to maintenance
Contact World Vision FMNR program: worldvision.com.au/fmnr

projects.name: PENGON — Palestinian Environmental Network
partners: Friends of the Earth Middle East
projects.description: Network of 29 Palestinian environmental organizations coordinating community solar, water harvesting, and ecological restoration under occupation. Operates in West Bank and Gaza despite extreme resource restrictions.
how_to_replicate: Under occupation/conflict: prioritize off-grid solar — no grid dependence means no Israeli control over power
Partner with PENGON for technical training: pengon.net
Apply for EU Neighborhood funding and UNDP Palestine grants
Rainwater harvesting cisterns: 50,000-liter concrete cisterns cost ~$2,000 and serve a family for years
Seed libraries protect food sovereignty — register seeds locally, exchange freely
Documentation is resistance: photograph and map every installation for international solidarity

projects.name: SunBox — Solar for Gaza Hospitals
projects.description: Emergency solar installations powering Gaza hospitals under siege. When Israeli forces cut grid power, solar kept ICUs, dialysis machines, and surgical theaters running. SolarPunk as survival technology.
how_to_replicate: For conflict/disaster response: prioritize hospital + water pump solar first
Portable solar kits (2-5kW): deployable in hours, no installation permit needed
Lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4) batteries — safer in conflict zones than lead-acid
Train local technicians before crisis — solar skills are life-saving infrastructure
Partner with MSF, IRC, or Oxfam for conflict-zone solar deployment protocols
Donate to verified Gaza solar campaigns via UNRWA or Islamic Relief

projects.name: Noor Atlas — Morocco Community Solar
projects.description: Morocco's rural electrification program powered 8,000 villages with solar home systems and mini-grids. 400,000 households. 60% cheaper than diesel alternatives. Now exporting model to 12 African nations.
how_to_replicate: Solar home systems (SHS): 50-200W panel + battery + LED lights for $200-400 per household
Work with national utility (ONEE-model) to create off-grid rural electrification authority
Apply to World Bank ESMAP (Energy Sector Management Assistance Program) for funding
Train community-based technicians — target 1 trained tech per 50 homes
Fee-for-service model: $3-8/month per household covers maintenance and expansion
IRENA has full Noor Atlas toolkit at irena.org/publications

projects.name: Edinburgh Community Solar Co-op
projects.description: 450-member energy cooperative owns 750kW of solar across Edinburgh schools and community buildings. Members earn 5% annual dividend. Profits fund community energy projects.
how_to_replicate: Register as a Community Benefit Society (CBS) in UK — use Cooperatives UK templates
Identify publicly-owned rooftops: schools, leisure centres, community halls — lease them for £1/year
Issue community shares: minimum £250, maximum £100,000 — EIS tax relief makes it attractive
Apply for Community Energy England or Community Energy Scotland development grants
Use Sharenergy or Ethex platforms for share issuance — they handle FCA compliance
Power Purchase Agreement with school: sell electricity at 10% below grid rate — win-win
REScoop.eu has full European co-op formation guide

projects.name: REScoop.eu — European Community Energy Federation
projects.description: Federation of 1,500 community energy cooperatives across 23 European countries. 1.2 million citizen-members. 2.5GW of renewable capacity. Provides legal templates, lobbying, and knowledge sharing for any European community wanting to form an energy co-op.
how_to_replicate: Visit rescoop.eu — free formation guides for every EU country
Join REScoop as a member for €500/year — access all legal templates and peer network
European Energy Community Directive gives citizens the legal right to form energy communities
Apply for European Regional Development Fund (ERDF) grants for community energy
REScoop runs annual conference and online training — strong community of practice

projects.name: Repair Café Foundation — Global Network
projects.description: Global network of 2,500 community repair workshops. Trained volunteer fixers repair electronics, clothing, furniture, and appliances for free. 70% success rate. Saves 500,000 items/year from landfill. Anyone can start one.
how_to_replicate: Register at repaircafe.org — free starter kit with all guides, logos, and templates
Find a free venue: library, community centre, church hall — 2-4 hours, monthly
Recruit volunteer fixers: electricians, seamstresses, carpenters — post on local Facebook groups
Provide basic tools: soldering iron ($30), multimeter ($20), basic hand tools
No charge for repairs — donations welcome, pass hat round
First event: expect 20-30 visitors, 15-20 items. Grows by word of mouth.
Apply for small local council grant (£500-2000) for tools and promotion

projects.name: Brixton Pound — Community Currency, London
projects.description: Local currency that only works in Brixton businesses. 250 local shops accept B£. Keeps money circulating locally — £1 B£ generates £1.70 of local economic activity (vs 40p for national chains). Printable, digital, and B-Pay mobile versions.
how_to_replicate: Register a Community Interest Company (CIC) or charity for currency governance
Use Bristol Pound open-source software stack for digital version (free to license)
Print local currency notes: partner with a local printer, use tamper-proof paper
Recruit anchor businesses first: market, pub, pharmacy — give each 50 B£ to spend
Peg 1:1 to national currency — 100% backed reserve, users convert freely
Council tax discount for paying in local currency brings mass adoption
Contact Brixton Pound for full replication guide: brixtonpound.org

projects.name: Kara Solar — Achuar Solar Canoes, Ecuadorian Amazon
projects.description: Solar-electric canoes for the Achuar Indigenous Nation in the Ecuadorian Amazon. No roads — rivers are the highways. Solar canoes replaced gasoline engines, protecting the forest from oil extraction pressure while cutting costs 80%.
how_to_replicate: Identify existing boat-dependent communities on rivers, lakes, or coastlines
Convert outboard motor: 5kW electric motor + 5kWh LiFePO4 battery + 200W solar = ~50km range
Conversion cost: $4,000-8,000 USD — 3-4 year payback on gasoline savings
Train community boat builders to do the conversion — technical knowledge transfer is key
Solar charges during the day while moored — fish, farm, attend school with zero fuel cost
Contact Kara Solar for partnership: karasolar.com

projects.name: Cook Islands — 100% Renewable Energy Target
projects.description: Small Pacific island nation transitioning to 100% renewable energy. Rarotonga already at 95% solar+wind. Annual savings: $8M/year that previously went to imported diesel. Model for all Pacific island nations.
how_to_replicate: Islands under 5,000 people: 100% solar+storage is cost-competitive with diesel TODAY
Apply to ADB Pacific Energy program and New Zealand Aid for Pacific island funding
Use IRENA's island renewable energy toolkit at irena.org/islands
Hybrid inverters (Victron or SMA) for solar + wind + diesel backup integration
Community ownership model: cooperative owns the assets, municipality offtakes power
Start with the highest diesel-cost island — that's where savings are most compelling

projects.name: Vanuatu Rural Electrification — Pacific Solar Microgrids
projects.description: Pacific nation electrifying outer islands with solar microgrids. 150 villages, 8,000 households. Zero diesel. Cyclone-rated hardware. Community-managed fee collection system. UN Sustainable Energy for All champion nation.
how_to_replicate: Cyclone/disaster zones: use IEC-rated solar panels (200km/h wind resistance), concrete anchor foundations
Community fee collection: assign trusted local 'energy agent' who collects monthly fees and reports to cooperative
Prepaid solar meters (SteamaCo or Angaza) prevent non-payment without disconnection drama
Use lithium iron phosphate batteries — perform better in tropical heat than lead-acid
Apply to World Bank Universal Energy Access program
Contact Pacific Community (SPC) in Noumea for Pacific island solar technical support

projects.name: Ngawha Geothermal — Māori-Owned Power Station, New Zealand

metrics.model: Māori tribe owns and operates geothermal station on ancestral land

projects.description: 100% Māori-owned geothermal power station on ancestral Ngāti Rangi land. 25MW, powers 17,000 homes. Annual revenue $15M NZD goes to tribal development, education, and health programs.
how_to_replicate: Geothermal applies where volcanic/tectonic activity exists — map hot springs and fumaroles
For Indigenous communities: Treaty settlement processes often include energy rights — assert them
Feasibility: geothermal resource assessment costs $500K-2M but is essential before investment
Apply to NZ Green Investment Fund and Crown Infrastructure Partners for co-financing
Structure as tribal authority company — keeps profits within iwi governance
Revenue split model: 40% tribal distributions, 30% reinvestment, 20% education, 10% reserve

projects.name: Enspiral — Worker Self-Directed Ventures, New Zealand
projects.description: Network of worker-directed ventures that collectively share revenue, governance, and infrastructure. Created Loomio (open-source decision-making used by 2M+ people) and Cobudget. Model for distributed cooperative economy.
how_to_replicate: Read the Enspiral Handbook — fully open-source at handbook.enspiral.com
Start with a core crew of 5-10 people who trust each other and share values
Use Loomio for all decisions (free for open-source groups): loomio.com
Collective fund: each member contributes 5-20% of revenue to shared pool
Cobudget: democratic allocation of collective funds — everyone votes with real dollars
No bosses: all strategic decisions require consent from all members
Annual retreat for in-person alignment — worth the cost

projects.name: BBOXX — Off-Grid Solar, East Africa
projects.description: Pay-as-you-go solar home systems for off-grid households in Africa and Asia. 350,000 customers. $0.30/day — less than a candle. Financed over 18-36 months, then owned outright. IoT-enabled for remote monitoring.
how_to_replicate: Solar home system components: 30-80W panel, 10-30Ah LiFePO4 battery, LED lights, phone charger — ~$100-200
PAYG model: mobile money payments (M-Pesa, MTN MoMo) — customer pays daily/weekly until ownership
Use Angaza or Solaris platform for PAYG management and remote cutoff ($0.05/customer/month)
Partner with mobile money operators early — airtime + solar bundle increases uptake
Train local solar agents for last-mile sales — commission-based, work in their own communities
Apply to IFC (World Bank) PAYG solar lending facility for working capital

projects.name: German Energiewende — 900+ Energy Cooperatives
projects.description: Germany's 900+ citizen energy cooperatives own 4.7GW of renewable energy — 13% of Germany's renewable capacity. Average cooperative: 220 members, €1,500 minimum investment. Model for citizen ownership of the energy transition.
how_to_replicate: German legal form: eG (eingetragene Genossenschaft) — use DGRV templates: dgrv.de
Citizen investment: €500-5,000 minimum, 3-5% annual return, EIS equivalent tax relief
Focus on community assets: local wind, rooftop solar on public buildings, biogas
Feed-in tariff + power purchase agreement = guaranteed revenue for 20 years
Apply to German federal community energy program (Bürgerenergiegesetz funds)
Key network: Bürgerenergie Berlin and AEE for support: unendlich-viel-energie.de

projects.name: Guifi.net — World's Largest Community Network

metrics.governance: Procomuns license — use it, improve it, give back

projects.description: 42,000-node community network spanning Catalonia, Valencia and the Balearics — the largest community-owned telecoms network in the world. Runs on the Procomuns license: use it, extend it, contribute back. Zero cost for members who contribute capacity. 20 years of proven operation.
how_to_replicate: Register as a foundation or cooperative — Guifi.net uses a non-profit foundation model
Adopt the Wireless Commons License or Procomuns — open access, reciprocal sharing requirement
Start with 10 founding node owners who each buy one WiFi antenna ($50-200)
Use free firmware: LibreMesh or OpenWRT — flash existing routers, no new hardware needed
Add 50W solar panel + 12Ah battery to remote nodes for 24h energy independence
Connect to peering points: negotiate with ISPs for uplink or build community dark fiber
Scale: each new node extends the network at zero marginal infrastructure cost

projects.name: AlterMundi — Rural Community Networks, Argentina
projects.description: AlterMundi builds community networks in rural Argentina where commercial internet never arrives, and developed LibreMesh firmware now used by 100+ communities in 40 countries. Each network is community-owned — no telecom landlord. $2/month covers uplink and hardware. Solar nodes extend coverage to off-grid farmsteads.
how_to_replicate: Download LibreMesh firmware (libremesh.org) — free, open-source, runs on $30 routers
Form a local network assembly — 5+ households elect a council, set prices democratically
Buy LibreRouter hardware (~$150) or flash existing Ubiquiti or TP-Link routers
Install 50W solar on any rooftop node — 12Ah LiFePO4 battery = weather independent
Negotiate bulk fiber uplink with regional ISP — 10 communities pooling = 10x buying power
Register as a social cooperative under local law for legal protection
Email redes@altermundi.net — they send a free community replication guide

projects.name: Rhizomatica / TIC — Indigenous Cellular Networks, Mexico
partners: Ministry of Communications and Transportation Mexico
projects.description: 75 indigenous communities in Oaxaca and Guerrero own and operate their own cellular telephone networks at $1.50/month — 95% cheaper than commercial carriers. Rhizomatica helped communities win the first indigenous-owned spectrum licenses in Mexican history. Solar-powered base stations. No telecom company. No landlord. Community-owned signal.
how_to_replicate: Form a community telecom cooperative — needs 5+ founding members and legal registration
Apply for community spectrum license — Rhizomatica has template legal documents for Mexico, Ecuador, and South Africa
Install OpenBTS or Osmocom base station ($3,000-8,000) — one station covers 1-3 villages
Mount base station on church tower, water tower, or community building with line-of-sight
Add 200W solar + 100Ah LiFePO4 battery — runs 72h without sun
Charge $1.50-2/month — covers hardware maintenance and spectrum license fees
Email info@rhizomatica.org — free technical assistance available

sources.title: WIRED: The Villages That Built Their Own Cell Network

projects.name: AirJaldi — Mountain WiFi Cooperative, Himachal Pradesh
projects.description: Long-distance WiFi cooperative connecting 200+ villages in the Himalayas and 7 Indian states using directional antennas that bridge 40-80km mountain passes where cable is impossible. 250,000+ people connected at $3/month. Solar-powered relay stations. Operating since 2009 — one of the world's longest-running rural community networks.
how_to_replicate: Survey terrain with Google Earth — identify high points for relay towers (peaks, ridges, water towers)
Use Ubiquiti airMax or MikroTik for long-distance point-to-point links (40-80km range)
Power remote relay stations with 100W solar + 200Ah battery — no grid dependency
Form a rural cooperative under local law — panchayat council support is essential
Apply for Universal Service Obligation Fund (USOF) grants for rural connectivity subsidies
Charge $3-5/month per household — cross-subsidize poorest households from surplus
Contact AirJaldi for training and mentorship: info@jaldi.org.in

projects.name: Fantsuam Foundation — Solar + Community Internet, Nigeria
projects.description: Nigeria's first rural community ISP, 100% solar-powered. The network earns revenue that funds West Africa's most successful rural women's ICT training program — 5,000+ women trained. Zero fossil fuel dependency. The internet pays for the training. The training creates new operators. The loop never stops.
how_to_replicate: Register as NGO or social enterprise — Fantsuam uses NGO status for tax exemption and donor eligibility
Install 3-5kW solar array + battery bank first — energy independence before internet infrastructure
Set up tower + directional antenna + LibreRouter mesh nodes for last-mile distribution
Apply for ISP license from national regulator — community license tier costs less
Pair internet access with digital training programs — the network funds the training
Target women specifically: digital literacy creates economic independence in rural settings
Contact APC for West Africa support: apc.org/en/contact

projects.name: Kopernik — Last Mile Solar, Indonesia & East Timor
projects.description: 240,000+ solar units distributed to isolated island and jungle communities in Indonesia, East Timor, and Tanzania through a network of women micro-entrepreneurs who buy wholesale and sell on PAYG credit. 1.2M+ people reached. The model: women entrepreneurs ARE the distribution network — no corporate middleman.
how_to_replicate: Map off-grid communities using WorldPop and OpenStreetMap — identify density and access routes
Recruit women entrepreneurs in market towns as last-mile distributors — 5-10% margin on each unit
Source solar lanterns and SHSs wholesale: d.light, Greenlight Planet, or BBOXX at $10-150
Offer PAYG credit: small first payment + weekly or monthly top-up via mobile money
Train distributors on solar basics + financial record-keeping (1 day training is enough)
Apply for USAID Development Innovation Ventures or Shell Foundation Energy Access grants
Contact Kopernik for partnership model: kopernik.info/partner

projects.name: NYC Mesh — People's Internet, New York City
projects.description: 1,400-node community-owned mesh network across all 5 NYC boroughs. Pay $20/month if you can, free if you cannot. 500+ buildings connected. Survived Hurricane Sandy when commercial internet failed. Built entirely by volunteers, governed by members. Urban rooftop-to-apartment = 300Mbps. Solidarity pricing: ability to pay never determines access.
how_to_replicate: Form a nonprofit (501c3 or equivalent) — allows tax-deductible donations and grant eligibility
Install first supernodes on tall buildings with city-wide line of sight
Use Ubiquiti or MikroTik rooftop antennas for node-to-node links
Reach each apartment via ethernet from rooftop to indoor router
Adopt solidarity pricing: suggested amount, never deny access for inability to pay
Peer with other ISPs at local internet exchange for cheap upstream bandwidth
Copy NYC Mesh's full playbook: docs.nycmesh.net — open source, copy freely
